newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Rally revives in U.S. T-bond futures.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Rally revives in U.S. T-bond futures.

text.p: U.S. Treasury bond futures' two-month recovery showed new resolve Thursday after weak May retail sales propelled prices to their highest levels since late February.

September bond futures broke a three-day slump that followed Friday's post-jobs report rally, bursting through that day's high of 111-09 to reach 111-15 this morning before stalling. The contract was last trading at 111-13, up 26/32.
Technicians were targeting various levels above the market, from 112-00 up through the February 18 peak of 113-09, as next price objectives.
But they also said prices would lurch rather than glide higher, given the recent pattern of fits and starts.

"It's certainly not a runaway market. We seem to move up, consolidate and move up again," said Jim Bohan, senior financial futures strategist for Merrill Lynch Capital Markets, who nonetheless expected prices to challenge the February highs.
"You have to be positive," he said. "I think the uptrend is pretty strong. This is a fairly dynamic move in the financial markets."
To maintain momentum, September bonds need to stay above 110-16 to 110-12, encompassing lows from the past several days, Bohan said.
"We should not come below that level now if this breakout is going to be validated," he said.

David Lundgren, senior technical analyst at Technical Data, said 111-15, the session high so far, represented the top of an ascending channel drawn from the May 2 high and therefore posed tough resistance. The level also corresponds with an upper Bollinger band identified through moving average analysis, he said.
That said, Lundgren also forecast more gains for bond futures, predicting September would climb to 113-09 in the next week or two.
"It would be tough to imagine that the trend is going to stop at the channel," he said, adding that a close above 111-15 would jump-start the move.

Greg Troccoli, director of technical trade strategy for Prudential Securities Inc, said 112-00 was his measured upside projection based on this week's flag formation that had Friday's rally as its pole.
Most importantly, he said, September bonds last week broke above the downtrend line drawn from the December highs and have since traveled a good distance above it. The trendline now falls at 109-27.
It would take a close below 110-17 for the rally to falter now, Troccoli said.
